newsitem.title: USA: Judge refuses to dismiss suit vs Gaylord.
newsitem.headline: Judge refuses to dismiss suit vs Gaylord.

text.p: A Delaware judge has refused a request by Gaylord Container Corp to dismiss a shareholder lawsuit alleging that the Gaylord board adopted takeover defenses in order to entrench itself.

In a nine-page opinion made available to Reuters Monday, Vice Chancellor Bernard Balick of Delaware Chancery Court said he needed more information before deciding whether "the board took proper precautions from coercive takeover tactics or, as the plaintiffs claim, acted primarily to keep control."
At issue is a bankruptcy reorganization plan that would reduce the voting power of the Gaylord board and of its founder-chairman Marvin Pomerantz from 72 percent to 20 percent.
In a proxy statement, the board said it adopted charter and bylaw amendments "to increase the effectiveness of a shareholder rights (poison pill) plan," according to court documents.
The shareholder plaintiffs allege the changes were made to fend off reported takeover interest by unspecified companies.
Gaylord, a manufacturer of brown paper and related packaging products, is based in Deerfield, Ill.
Company officials could not be reached for comment on the court decision.
